A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same ModHiFi study and Appendices A-E. Text, equations, tables and figures can be matched. Although v1 clips the lower panels and caption of Figure 3, these remain recoverable from its embedded PDF content and match v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original pruning and classwise-unlearning experiments, fidelity analyses and ablations in Section 5 and Appendices B-C.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, fidelity analyses and ablations, including the empirical results in its appendices.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1-2 and Appendix D retain the same fidelity-based component selection, compensated pruning, class-specific editing and Cholesky-based LLM scoring. The expanded mask formulation does not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions retain CIFAR-10/100 and ImageNet vision experiments, WikiText-2 and Alpaca calibration, and the same language evaluations including ARC, PIQA, WinoGrande and HellaSwag. The reformatted Figure 3 contains existing experiments rather than added coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same comparator rows: GReg-2, OTO, DepGRAPH, ThiNet, DFPC and L2 variants for vision pruning; SliceGPT and ShortGPT for LLM pruning; and Gradient Ascent, Jia et al. and DisCEdit-U in their respective unlearning experiments.

E3.justification: The LLM calibration setting of 128 samples of length 1024, evaluation metrics, pruning levels and training budgets are unchanged. The three- and ten-epoch unlearning fine-tuning comparisons and Appendix C.7 training procedures are also retained.

E4.justification: The same Monte Carlo fidelity analysis, component-removal counterfactuals, sample-size and noise robustness tests, synthetic-data-quality study, BatchNorm/compensation ablation and Lipschitz-constant analysis appear in both versions. Figure rearrangements do not introduce new analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix C.1.3 retains three random seeds per sampled data size and error bars. The boxplots and uncertainty displays are retained, with no added run counts or statistical estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Figures 2 and 10 change the trained ResNet-50/CIFAR-10 accuracy in their legends from 76.1 to 94.99, aligning them with the existing tables. The plotted curves and benchmark table values remain unchanged; this is a reporting correction, not evidence of improved performance.

T1.justification: Section 2.2 revises the formal pruning constraint to explicit group-selection gates with real-valued compensation. Corollary B.4 changes its norm lower-bound assumption from almost surely over the data distribution to 'for all x.' The central local-to-global and singleton-optimality results and proof arguments are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: local-to-global fidelity reasoning, optimal singleton selection under uncorrelated features, and unified pruning/unlearning using distributional access. The 11% ImageNet speedup and unlearning claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations of HiFi components, synthetic-data quality and Swin-T unlearning remain the same. Discussion of well-trained networks, imperfect feature independence, fine-tuning outside the primary assumptions and alternative future similarity metrics is retained; the limitations paragraph is moved and copyedited.

D1.justification: Checklist item 5 newly states that dataset-acquisition instructions are provided in the existing GitHub repository. This is a limited access-guidance addition; the repository URL, dataset links, hardware, hyperparameters and implementation details are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning in Section 2.3 and Appendix A are unchanged. Both versions present ModHiFi as a unified framework distinguished from architecture-specific pruning and training-data-dependent unlearning methods.

P1.justification: v2 copyedits the abstract and main narrative, expands the problem-formulation explanation, clarifies global-error terminology and adds a brief sketch for Theorem 3.9. The overall section sequence and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The appendix figures undergo substantial relayout: Figure 3 changes from an overflowing vertical stack to a fully visible two-column arrangement, and Figures 8-10 change from vertical stacks to four-column grids. Former Figures 11 and 12 become panels of Figure 11. Noise plots are redrawn, and tables and other figures are repositioned.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects the inaccurate trained-model legends, restores visibility of the complete Figure 3 and clarifies the grouped-mask formulation and prose. These improve reporting consistency and readability. The algorithms and experimental support remain unchanged, while Corollary B.4 imposes a stronger premise rather than extending theoretical coverage, so the overall gain is limited.
